newsitem.title: USA: Amoco to expand polypropylene capacity.
newsitem.headline: Amoco to expand polypropylene capacity.

text.p: Amoco Corp said it plans to expand its global polypropylene manufacturing capacity by 330,000 tons per year.
Amoco Polymers will increase polypropylene capacity by 250,000 tons per year at its 550,000 ton per year Chocolate Bayou chemical plant near Alvin, Texas.
"The expansion will bring Amoco's total North American polypropylene capacity to about 1.1 million tons per year," the energy and chemicals giant said.
The project, expected to be completed by early 1999, will add about 40 employees to the Chocolate Bayou facility.

Amoco Chemical Europe is proceeding with plans to improve production efficiencies, or "debottleneck", its 200,000 ton per year polypropylene plant in Geel, Belgium. The project will bring total Western European polypropylene capacity to 490,000 tons per year, Amoco said.
Costs of the projects were not identified.
Amoco was the world's second largest polypropylene producer in 1996 with a production capacity of about 1.2 million tons, the company said.
Polypropylene is used in a wide variety of plastics and fibers including appliances, packaging, automotive components, and carpet yarns and backing.
